title: What Is a Current Account Deficit — and Why It Matters for Indonesia
excerpt: A current account deficit is one of the most watched macro variables in emerging markets.
body: The current account is the broadest measure of a country's transactions with the rest of the world.
When a country spends more on imports than it earns from exports, it runs a current account deficit. This is not inherently bad.
For Indonesia, the current account has become a focal point for investors and policymakers alike.

title: CPhttp://76.13.17.91/images/IMG-20260424-WA0029-13a8ddf616a6.jpgI vs. Core Inflation: Why Central Banks Watch the Difference
excerpt: Headline inflation captures everything. Core inflation tells you what the central bank really cares about.
body: Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation is the number that makes headlines.
Core inflation strips out the most volatile components: food prices and administered prices.
When core inflation falls below 2.5% and is on a stable downward path, BI has room to begin easing.

title: JCI at 7,200: Why BI's Rate Hold Changes the Playbook
excerpt: With Bank Indonesia holding rates and the Fed signaling caution, the calculus for Indonesian equities has shifted.
body: The Jakarta Composite Index's push toward 7,200 this quarter reflects resilient corporate earnings and foreign inflow momentum.
Bank Indonesia's decision to hold the BI Rate at 6.00% removes one tail risk from the equity market.
However, the external backdrop remains challenging.

title: How We Build Our Macro Models: A Behind-the-Scenes Look
excerpt: Our GDP nowcasting model combines official data, high-frequency indicators, and machine learning.
body: One of the most challenging problems in emerging market research is the lag between what is happening and what official data reveals.
This is the nowcasting problem — and it's where we spend a significant portion of our analytical effort.
We validate this model continuously against new official releases and publish our nowcast alongside each BPS release.

title: Prospek Makro Indonesia 2026: Menavigasi Angin Keringat Global
excerpt: Dengan pertumbuhan global melambat, fundamental makroekonomi Indonesia tetap tangguh.
body: Indonesia memasuki 2026 dengan salah satu profil makro paling tangguh di Asia Tenggara.
Pendorong utama ketahanan ini adalah konsumsi rumah tangga yang kuat, yang menyumbang sekitar 57% PDB.
Risiko utama meliputi pelemahan IDR jika The Fed menunda pemotongan suku bunga.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Dominance: The EV Supply Chain Power Play
excerpt: Indonesia controls 22% of global nickel reserves. Here's how it became the world's battery manufacturing hub.
body: Indonesia's strategic move to ban raw nickel ore exports in 2020 was controversial. Three years later, the strategy is paying off spectacularly.
By forcing foreign investment in domestic processing, Indonesia attracted over $15 billion in EV battery and smelter investments.
HPAL (High Pressure Acid Leach) plants now dot the Sulawesi coastline, processing laterite ore into nickel sulphate for lithium-ion batteries.

title: Indonesia's Digital Economy: Why 2026 Is the Inflection Point
excerpt: With 220 million internet users and a $40B GMV target, Indonesia's digital economy is entering a new phase.
body: Indonesia's digital economy has grown at a compound annual growth rate of 22% since 2021.
The government's Making Indonesia 4.0 roadmap targets 22% contribution to GDP by 2030.
Fintech, e-commerce, and super-apps continue to drive growth, while enterprise SaaS adoption is accelerating among SMEs.

title: Understanding G20's New Bank Capital Rules and What They Mean for Indonesian Banks
excerpt: Basel III endgame rules will reshape how Indonesian banks allocate capital. Here's a practical guide.
body: Bank Indonesia has begun implementing Basel III endgame capital standards that will require major banks to hold more capital against risk-weighted assets.
For Indonesian banks, the primary impact will be on mortgage lending, where risk weights for property exposures will increase.
We estimate that the largest four banks — BCA, BRI, Mandiri, BNI — will need to raise a combined Rp 120 trillion in Tier-1 capital.

title: Downstreaming Nikel Indonesia: Dari Raw Ore ke Baterai Kendaraan Listrik
excerpt: Strategi hilirisasi nikel telah menarik investasi Rp 230 triliun dan menciptakan ekosistem industri baterai kendaraan listrik.
body: Larangan ekspor bijih nikel mentah pada 2020 adalah langkah berani yang kini membuahkan hasil.
Pabrik-pabrik HPAL (High Pressure Acid Leach) kini berdiri di Sulawesi, memproses ore laterit menjadi nikel sulfat untuk baterai litium-ion.
Invetsasi dari TSLA-backed CATL, LG Energy Solution, dan Hyundai menciptakan rantai pasok kendaraan listrik terintegrasi.

title: Menggenggam Inflasi Harga Pangan: Dari Petani hingga Konsumen
excerpt: Inflasi pangan volatile. AndaraLab menganalisis mekanisme transmisinya dan kebijakan stabilisasi harga yang efektif.
body: Inflasi harga pangan menyumbang sekitar 30-40% dari total inflasi IHK di Indonesia.
Volatilitas ini terutama didorong oleh faktor musiman produksi pertanian dan gangguan cuaca.
AndaraLab mengembangkan model prediktif untuk memperkirakan pergerakan harga pangan 4-6 minggu ke depan.

title: Mengapa Ekonomi Digital Indonesia adalah Pasar Terbesar di Asia Tenggara
excerpt: Dengan GMV yang ditargetkan mencapai $360 miliar pada 2030, ekonomi digital Indonesia adalah ladang riset utama.
body: Indonesia menyumbang 35% dari total GMV ekonomi digital ASEAN.
E-commerce, fintech, dan super-apps menjadi mesin pertumbuhan utama.
Adopsi SaaS enterprise di kalangan UMKM mulai mempercepat transformasi digital.

title: Omnibus Law Two Years Later: What the Data Actually Shows
excerpt: After two years of the Job Creation Law, we examine whether it delivered on its investment and employment promises.
body: The Job Creation Law (UU Cipta Kerja) was Indonesia's most significant regulatory overhaul in decades.
Initial data on foreign direct investment shows a 12% increase in approved investments in the 18 months following its passage.
However, formal employment growth has been modest, and the law's impact on labor market dynamics remains contested.

title: Indonesia Government Bond Market Outlook H1 2026
excerpt: With a record Rp 890 trillion in net financing needed, the SUN market faces a pivotal first half.
body: Indonesia's government bond market is entering a critical period with significant refinancing needs.
Foreign ownership of government bonds stands at 15.2% — down from the 40% peak in 2019 but still a meaningful market share.
We expect yield curve steepening in Q1 2026 as BI holds rates while fiscal issuance accelerates.

title: Indonesia's Progressive Tax Reform Agenda for 2026
excerpt: Draft legislation proposes a new progressive personal income tax bracket that could reshape household consumption patterns.
body: The Ministry of Finance has published draft legislation proposing a revised PPh Article 25 bracket structure.
For high-income earners (above Rp 5 billion annually), effective tax rates would increase from 30% to 35%.
The reform is expected to generate Rp 25 trillion in additional annual revenue.

title: The Future of Indonesia's Nickel Downstreaming in the EV Era
excerpt: Indonesia, yang memiliki cadangan nikel terbesar di dunia, telah bergerak agresif untuk melarang ekspor bijih mentah dan membangun basis industri dalam negeri.
body: Nickel is at the heart of the global transition to electric vehicles. Indonesia, holding the world's largest nickel reserves, has moved aggressively to ban raw ore exports and build a domestic industrial base.
The 2020 nickel ore export ban was a watershed moment. By forcing foreign investors to process ore domestically, Indonesia attracted over $15 billion in downstream investment within three years.
Today, Indonesia's HPAL plants produce nickel sulphate — the key input for EV battery cathodes — at scale, positioning Indonesia as a critical node in the global EV supply chain.
As EV adoption accelerates globally, Indonesia's leverage over battery manufacturers and automakers will only grow.

title: Global Fertilizer Supply Tightens as Russia Extends Export Limits on Hormuz Disruptions
excerpt:
- Russia extends fertilizer export limits through year-end, tightening global supply
- Hormuz disruptions cut roughly one-third of seaborne fertilizer flows
- Major producers, including Russia and China, curb exports as shortages worsen
- Nitrogen fertilizer prices have nearly doubled since February
- Rising costs could pressure farmers and increase global food inflation risk
body: Global fertilizer supplies are tightening once again, as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and ongoing geopolitical tensions continue to pressure international markets. The situation is raising concerns that rising input costs could eventually translate into higher food prices worldwide.

Russia has announced an extension of its fertilizer export limits through the end of the year, adding further strain to an already constrained global supply. Under the new policy, Russian producers will be allowed to export up to 20 million tonnes between June 1 and November 30. This follows an earlier quota of 18.7 million tonnes that remains in place until late May, with domestic farmers benefiting from subsidized pricing.

The move comes at a time when the global fertilizer market is already facing significant disruptions. Bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for agricultural trade, have reduced roughly one-third of global seaborne fertilizer flows. As countries scramble to secure alternative supplies, major producers such as Russia and China have also limited exports, further tightening availability and pushing prices higher.

As one of the world’s largest fertilizer suppliers, accounting for around 20 percent of global trade, Russia is increasingly prioritizing domestic agricultural needs over international demand. This shift is aimed at protecting local farmers from rising costs but is adding pressure to global markets that rely heavily on its exports.

The newly announced export quota includes approximately 8.7 million tonnes of nitrogen-based fertilizers, more than 4.2 million tonnes of ammonium nitrate, and around 7 million tonnes of compound fertilizers.
[IMG: /images/Gemini_Generated_Image_cbza8ycbza8ycbza-e57ec8b43b33.png]
Certain shipments will remain exempt from these restrictions, including deliveries to pro-Russia separatist territories, goods already in transit, and supplies designated for humanitarian purposes.

Meanwhile, fertilizer prices have already surged in recent months. Nitrogen fertilizer costs have nearly doubled since the Iran conflict escalated in February. If disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz persist, analysts warn that prices could rise even further.

Higher costs may eventually force farmers to reduce fertilizer usage, which could impact crop yields and tighten global food supply. As a result, the current supply squeeze is not only a concern for agricultural markets but also a potential risk factor for global food inflation in the months ahead.

title: Rusia Perpanjang Pembatasan Ekspor di Tengah Gangguan Hormuz, Pasokan Pupuk Global Menipis
excerpt:
- Rusia memperpanjang pembatasan ekspor pupuk hingga akhir tahun, memperketat pasokan global
- Gangguan di Selat Hormuz memangkas sekitar sepertiga aliran pupuk laut global
- Produsen besar, termasuk Rusia dan China, membatasi ekspor saat kelangkaan memburuk
- Harga pupuk nitrogen hampir dua kali lipat sejak Februari
- Kenaikan biaya berpotensi menekan petani dan meningkatkan risiko inflasi pangan global
body: Pasokan pupuk global kembali mengetat, seiring gangguan di Selat Hormuz dan ketegangan geopolitik yang terus menekan pasar internasional. Kondisi ini memicu kekhawatiran bahwa kenaikan biaya input pada akhirnya dapat mendorong kenaikan harga pangan secara global.

Rusia mengumumkan perpanjangan pembatasan ekspor pupuk hingga akhir tahun, yang semakin menambah tekanan pada pasokan global yang sudah terbatas. Dalam kebijakan terbaru, produsen pupuk Rusia diizinkan mengekspor hingga 20 juta ton dalam periode 1 Juni hingga 30 November. Kebijakan ini menyusul kuota sebelumnya sebesar 18,7 juta ton yang berlaku hingga akhir Mei, di mana petani domestik mendapatkan pupuk dengan harga subsidi.

Langkah ini diambil di tengah kondisi pasar pupuk global yang sudah menghadapi gangguan signifikan. Hambatan di Selat Hormuz, jalur penting bagi perdagangan input pertanian, telah mengurangi sekitar sepertiga pengiriman pupuk global melalui jalur laut. Di saat negara-negara berupaya mencari sumber pasokan alternatif, produsen besar seperti Rusia dan China juga membatasi ekspor, sehingga semakin memperketat ketersediaan dan mendorong harga naik.

Sebagai salah satu pemasok pupuk terbesar di dunia, dengan sekitar 20 persen pangsa perdagangan global, Rusia kini semakin memprioritaskan kebutuhan pertanian domestik dibandingkan permintaan internasional. Langkah ini bertujuan melindungi petani dalam negeri dari kenaikan biaya, namun di sisi lain menambah tekanan bagi pasar global yang sangat bergantung pada pasokan Rusia.
Kuota ekspor terbaru ini mencakup sekitar 8,7 juta ton pupuk berbasis nitrogen, lebih dari 4,2 juta ton amonium nitrat, serta sekitar 7 juta ton pupuk majemuk.

Namun, pembatasan ini tidak berlaku untuk beberapa jenis pengiriman, termasuk distribusi ke wilayah separatis yang pro-Rusia, barang yang sudah dalam proses pengiriman, serta pasokan yang dialokasikan untuk tujuan kemanusiaan.

Sementara itu, harga pupuk telah melonjak dalam beberapa bulan terakhir. Biaya pupuk nitrogen tercatat hampir dua kali lipat sejak konflik Iran meningkat pada Februari. Jika gangguan di Selat Hormuz terus berlanjut, analis memperkirakan harga masih berpotensi naik lebih lanjut.

Kenaikan biaya ini pada akhirnya dapat memaksa petani mengurangi penggunaan pupuk, yang berisiko menekan hasil panen dan memperketat pasokan pangan global. Akibatnya, tekanan pada pasokan pupuk saat ini tidak hanya menjadi isu di sektor pertanian, tetapi juga berpotensi memicu inflasi pangan global dalam beberapa bulan ke depan.

title: IHSG di 7.200: Mengapa Keputusan BI Tahan Suku Bunga Mengubah Strategi Pasar
excerpt: Dengan Bank Indonesia mempertahankan suku bunga dan The Fed memberi sinyal kehati-hatian, kalkulasi untuk saham Indonesia telah bergeser.
body: Dorongan Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) menuju level 7.200 pada kuartal ini mencerminkan ketahanan laba korporasi dan momentum aliran masuk modal asing yang masih solid.

Keputusan Bank Indonesia untuk mempertahankan BI Rate di level 6,00% menghilangkan satu risiko ekor dari pasar saham — investor tidak perlu lagi mengkhawatirkan tekanan likuiditas jangka pendek akibat kenaikan suku bunga domestik.

Namun, latar belakang eksternal tetap menantang. Ketidakpastian kebijakan moneter The Fed, tekanan nilai tukar rupiah, dan dinamika harga komoditas global masih menjadi variabel yang perlu dicermati investor.
Dari sisi sektoral, saham perbankan dan konsumer menjadi penopang utama kenaikan IHSG. Emiten dengan eksposur domestik yang kuat cenderung lebih resilient di tengah volatilitas global.

Untuk jangka pendek, level 7.200 menjadi resistance psikologis penting. Penembusan level ini secara konsisten akan membuka ruang kenaikan lebih lanjut menuju 7.400-7.500, dengan catatan aliran dana asing tetap positif dan data makro domestik tidak mengecewakan.
